summary: Nine compute-bound experiments occupied 71.4 wall-time minutes. The longest were evidence-set probability training at 25.83 minutes, archive replay separation at 15.58 minutes, and per-sentence normalization qualification at 13.42 minutes; the timing record does not explain which stages caused those durations.
bottlenecks_identified: The three longest compute-bound experiments account for 54.83 of 71.4 wall-time minutes. No stage timings identify why any one of them ran long.
The milestone clock was reconstructed from disk modification times because the live git-log path found 0 commits. Direct task start and finish receipts were unavailable.
The GPU report is a point-in-time view. It cannot establish utilization throughout the compute-bound runs, whether requests were batched, or whether any task loaded multiple models concurrently.
improvements_suggested: Write task receipts with monotonic start, finish, and stage durations so the next slow run can be attributed to a measured stage.
Sample GPU utilization and memory during each task, joined to process and task identifiers, and record overlapping model loads before evaluating DualGPURunner eligibility.
Run a bounded batching benchmark for independent GGUF questions and adopt a batch size only if measured throughput improves within memory limits.
Persist execution timestamps at task boundaries so milestone timing does not depend on disk modification times.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add stage timers and task-linked GPU samples to the execution receipt for evidence-set training and archive replay separation.
Measure GGUF throughput with and without batching before changing inference defaults.
Record task lifecycle timestamps and concurrent model loads so timing and DualGPURunner assessments can be verified.
meta_reflection: The GPU snapshot shows GPU 1 active at 97% and GPU 0 idle, but it does not measure utilization across task lifetimes. The supplied records do not establish whether a task had concurrent models, so a DualGPURunner miss cannot be determined. Savings cannot be quantified without timing an intervention against a baseline.
